summary.title: The Forge of Haron Sil: A Needle to Kill a God
summary.synopsis: The Weft restores power to a mysterious underground facility and discovers a nascent divine heart — a forge of unknown origin created by someone named Haron Sil. After a chaotic battle with incorporeal hazmat-suited creatures, Henrik discovers that Damien is actually hooked into the facility's control system and mercy-kills him. The party awakens the heart with Savick's Blood, then must plead their case before all five members of the Narrative to earn permission to forge a godpiercer needle from Holy Gold.
key_beats: The party lets Schism investigate the glowing core, discovering it's a 'baby heart' — a divine forge of unknown third-faction origin (not Sanctum or Thessian) that can create items from divine energy, potentially including Holy Gold.

After debating whether to wake the heart, the party fully charges the facility's power, triggering an arcane intelligence that announces godlike judgment. Six black-suited worker creatures and numerous smaller assistants emerge from the vents.

Combat begins against the creatures, who are incorporeal. The party learns the mechanics: killing assistants drops divine energy orbs, touching two orbs makes workers corporeal (a 'DPS phase'), but hitting the wrong worker during this phase causes damaging explosions.

Henrik opens Damien's door and discovers Damien is actually stuffed inside a hazmat suit, wired into the facility's pipes as a living control system. After a botched attempt, Henrik rips Damien free, killing him — which collapses all the workers and causes the facility's autonomous intelligence to resume control, draining the rising lava.
Divex and Lev use resonance crystals from the Solarium to collect ambient divine energy, producing three vials of Starsong Nectar.

The party pours four vials of Savick's Blood onto the heart, awakening it as a conscious entity that identifies itself as 'Damien.' Dawn presents Holy Gold and requests a godpiercer needle, but Damien says it needs permission from its 'owners.'

The party is transported to an endless white space where they meet all five members of the Narrative: Aut (the author), Renge (Lady of Fortune, tall hollow-eyed figure), P'ter (a living house of nested rooms), Menier (shifting stone pillars), and Insuperlex (a bisected humanoid showing cross-section organs).

The party argues for permission to forge the needle. Renge proposes restricting its use to within their story only. Aut counter-proposes giving a fragment to the Broker to create a new antagonist, but is voted down 2-2 with Aut outvoted.
Damien forges the godpiercer needle — a one-foot golden cone that renders divine beings mortal (vulnerability 25 to all damage, loses divine abilities). Dawn claims it.

Damien has 18 charges remaining and can create more items up to level 18. The party levels up to level 18. Discussion turns to Lev wanting a cool sword, the Broker's true motivations for wanting Formless, and Dawn privately telling Schism the needle is meant for the Broker, not Formless.
items: Savick's Blood (four vials, consumed to awaken heart)
summary.cliffhanger: Dawn secretly tells Schism the godpiercer needle isn't for Formless — it's for the Broker, who still wants the Formless shard. The party stands at the forge with 18 charges remaining and major decisions ahead, while the Broker's true motivations remain unknown.
